title: Database Ablation Study
body:
Overview

This record belongs to the Ablation and Feature Contribution Experiments Database (public edition), a database that tests which databases, generators, and tools actually add value, by removing one feature at a time and measuring the change. Database Ablation Study covers the following: measures the score change when one database is removed from the retrieval set. The record is written as a complete, usable file: it states what the entry is, how it is used, and what its limits are, and it carries a demo program that was genuinely executed at build time, with its output stored beside the code. Benchmark honesty: this database defines part of the fixed test suite for the R32 capability collection. Its target is 99% measured reliability on defined tasks (TARGET, not measured result). The comparative measurement run comes after building and is not claimed anywhere in this round.

How it works

An ablation run holds the task list and every other feature fixed, removes exactly one feature, and records the resulting score beside the full-configuration score, so the difference in score points is attributable to that one feature alone. Applied to this record, the method means the following in practice: measures the score change when one database is removed from the retrieval set. The record sits at ladder rank simple in the teaching ladder, which runs simple, then compounded, then most complex, so a reader can start from the simpler records and work toward this one.

Worked example

The demo compares a full configuration score with an ablated configuration score and prints the difference in score points. The demo program prints:

Full configuration score: 80 points
Ablated configuration score: 78 points
Feature contribution: 2 score points

Use and limits

Ablation scores describe the tested configuration only. Removing two features at once can behave differently from removing either alone, and interaction effects need their own dedicated studies. In practice, a reader can use this record to run the same check on their own tasks: follow the method, compare the result with the worked example, and record any difference with its evidence. The record is one of sixteen in this database, and it cross-links to related databases so the reader can continue from here without guessing where to look next.

Record details

Record fields: feature_removed: verification step; configuration: ablated configuration; metric: cost per task; task_class: retrieval of existing records.
demo_code:
full_score = 80
ablated_score = 78
contribution = full_score - ablated_score
print('Full configuration score: ' + str(full_score) + ' points')
print('Ablated configuration score: ' + str(ablated_score) + ' points')
print('Feature contribution: ' + str(contribution) + ' score points')
demo_output:
Full configuration score: 80 points
Ablated configuration score: 78 points
Feature contribution: 2 score points
